investigationRule: one independent variable changes at a time in every assessed comparison

difficultyLevels.description: the game identifies the variable to change
the learner chooses which variable should change
the learner designs the controlled trial
the learner determines which experiments distinguish competing explanations
the learner must support a claim with multiple trials and/or graphs

families.name: Calibration Run
families.primaryConcept: balanced versus unbalanced force and net-force reasoning
families.scienceQuestion: What is the net force on the cart, and how does the cart's motion reflect it?
families.independentVariable: two collinear applied forces (or one force versus none)
families.dependentVariable: resulting motion: rest, constant velocity, or accelerated motion
families.expectedRelationship: equal-and-opposite forces give Fnet = 0 and no change in motion; unequal opposing forces give a signed nonzero Fnet and a = Fnet/m directed toward the larger force
families.requiredEvidence: at least one balanced trial and one unbalanced trial compared on net force, acceleration, and resulting motion
misconceptions: balanced forces mean the object is stopped
a constant push means constant speed

families.name: Thruster Test
families.primaryConcept: greater applied force produces greater acceleration at constant mass
families.scienceQuestion: How does the change in the cart's motion depend on the applied force when mass is controlled?
families.expectedRelationship: at constant mass a = Fnet/m, so acceleration is proportional to force; doubling force doubles acceleration
families.requiredEvidence: two trials differing only in force with acceleration and/or the velocity-time slope compared, naming mass as the controlled variable
misconceptions: more force always means a bigger speed rather than a bigger change
a longer run means more force

graphRequirement.note: the mandated graph-interpretation requirement: the slope of the velocity-time graph is the acceleration

families.name: Cargo Load Test
families.primaryConcept: greater mass produces less acceleration at constant applied force
families.scienceQuestion: How does the change in motion depend on the cart's mass when the applied force is controlled?
families.expectedRelationship: at constant net force a = Fnet/m, so acceleration is inversely proportional to mass; doubling mass halves acceleration
families.requiredEvidence: two trials differing only in mass with acceleration compared and the applied force explicitly identified as controlled
misconceptions: a heavier cart always accelerates less for any reason, independent of force
changing mass and force together is still a controlled test

graphRequirement.note: a more curved position-time trace indicates greater acceleration; never the only path to the data

families.name: Mystery Cart Investigation
families.primaryConcept: diagnose one bounded hidden cause from controlled experimental evidence
families.scienceQuestion: Which of the bounded explanations is consistent with the experimental evidence?
families.dependentVariable: which bounded explanation the evidence supports
families.expectedRelationship: exactly one declared candidate cause is consistent with the controlled comparisons; each competing explanation predicts a distinguishable deficit pattern
families.requiredEvidence: at least two controlled comparisons that distinguish the candidate explanations; a single uncontrolled observation does not count
misconceptions: one anomalous observation is enough to name a cause
a comparison in which two variables changed can still isolate a cause
the cart is faulty because it is slower than a sibling measured under different conditions

graphRequirement.note: at least one variant requires overlaying two velocity-time traces to compare slopes; the semantic table exposes the same data

candidateCauses.manifestation: lower than expected acceleration at nominal force
candidateCauses.distinguishingTest: vary mass with force controlled; the anomalous trial matches the heavier-mass curve

candidateCauses.manifestation: lower than expected acceleration at nominal mass
candidateCauses.distinguishingTest: vary force at nominal mass; the anomalous trial matches the lower-force curve

candidateCauses.manifestation: lower than expected acceleration that tracks the declared resistive force
candidateCauses.distinguishingTest: compare a run with the resistive force declared zero against one with it declared

candidateCauses.manifestation: every trial matches the nominal model within tolerance
candidateCauses.distinguishingTest: every controlled comparison matches prediction within tolerance
